judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are P2 Knowledge Objectives in the same Topic Area (Numbers and Operations) / Sub-Topic Area (Whole Numbers), so grain matches. The first reads 'Read and write numbers to the extend up to 200 in numerals and words' under Unit 1 (Numbers 0-200, Key Unit Competence to 200); the second reads 'Read and write numbers to the extent of 1000 in numerals and words' under Unit 3 (Numbers 0-1000, Key Unit Competence to 1000). This is not mere repetition: the identical read/write-in-numerals-and-words skill is extended to a substantially larger number range (three-digit numbers through 1000), so fluency in reading and writing numerals and number words to 200 supports success with the same skill to 1000. Coordinate rank is equal (P2 for both), but the unit-scoped range extension within the grade provides the substantive same-rank evidence for the first-to-second direction. Both endpoints carry upstream merge/audit context and truncated source evidence (24 omitted items each); the visible statements and LCs are nonetheless unambiguous on the range difference.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are P2 Knowledge Objectives (same statement-type grain, same Grade rank 1). The first (Unit 2, Whole Numbers, Key Unit Competence 0–500) asks pupils to explain how to add and subtract whole numbers to 500; the second (Unit 7, Mass Measurements 'Kg') asks pupils to explain how to add, subtract, multiply and divide mass measurements in kg, up to 10 kg per its Key Unit Competence. Explaining computation with kg quantities applies the same whole-number addition/subtraction reasoning in a measurement context, so proficiency with the number-operation explanations supports success with the measurement-quantity explanations; the second also extends to multiplication and division and to a measured-quantity referent, evidencing a forward developmental direction rather than mere repetition. Same-rank direction is grounded in this conceptual application relation (number operations applied to mass units), not on shared Grade, shared LC tokens ('add', 'subtract', 'explain') or later Unit position alone. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and both carry upstream audit/merge context, so the judgment rests on the full, untruncated objective statements and LCs supplied.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Knowledge Objectives (same statement-type grain) under TOPIC AREA: ALGEBRA, with resolved coordinates P1 (rank 0) and P2 (rank 1), so any developmental direction runs first_to_second. The P1 objective has pupils discover the ratio/interval between two consecutive numbers in a number pattern, sitting under the Key Unit Competence 'Finding the missing number in a number pattern ... 1 or 2 digits'. The P2 objective asks pupils to explain the rule used when finding missing numbers in addition, subtraction, multiplication and division, under Unit 12 'Missing numbers in addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division'. The later statement extends the same underlying idea — identifying and articulating the numerical rule that determines an unknown value — from the additive/multiplicative step within a sequence to explicit operation rules (including, per its LCs, separate rules for each of the four operations) and raises the demand from discovering to explaining. Prior facility with detecting the interval/rule between numbers plausibly supports success in stating the rule for a missing term in an operation, so a non-mandatory buildsTowards is supported rather than mere shared Algebra wording ('number', 'used', 'the'). Note the differing sub-topic areas (Number Pattern vs Equations) and truncated source/LC evidence temper confidence.

judgment.rationale: Both are P2 Knowledge Objectives (same grain, same rank P2) under Unit 9 'Hours, Months of the Year, and Days in Each Month' in the Time Measurements sub-topic. The first states 'Telling the time at exact hour, quarter past and half past' with LCs on reading clock faces/watches at o'clock, quarter past and half past; the second states 'Explain how to plan daily and weekly activities as well as time management' with LCs on planning daily/weekly activities and managing time. Reading and naming clock times is the enabling knowledge that makes scheduling activities and explaining time management meaningful, so proficiency in the first substantively supports success in the second; the second is an applied extension rather than a prerequisite for clock reading. Same-rank direction is grounded in this conceptual dependency, not in source page or table-row order, and shared Unit/Topic/LC 'time' overlap alone was not treated as sufficient. judgment.rationale: Both are same-grain Skills Objectives in P2 (rank 1), Unit 10 'Types of lines and angles', under the Key Unit Competence 'identify and draw different types of lines, acute and obtuse angles'. The second SFI has pupils illustrate straight, closed, open, curved and zigzag/broken lines in real objects in and outside the classroom; the first has pupils identify right, acute and obtuse angles formed by those same real objects. Angles are constituted by intersecting straight lines, so fluency in recognising and illustrating line types in environmental objects substantively supports the later, more complex task of classifying the angles those lines form; the source table also places the line objective (row 5) before the angle objective (row 6) within the same unit, and the KUC names lines before angles. Same-rank direction is therefore grounded in this pair-specific conceptual dependency, not merely shared parent, Unit, Topic Area 'Geometry' LC tag, or the generic wording overlap ('located in and outside the classroom') flagged by the nomination. The first requires recognizing and identifying Rwandan currency denominations (notes and coins); the second requires representing the same amount of money in different denominations, i.e. composing/decomposing an equivalent value across those denominations. Knowing and identifying the individual denominations is the substantive knowledge on which equivalent-value representation depends, so proficiency in the first supports success in the second (same P3 rank, but the content change is a step from identification to equivalence/representation, consistent with adjacent source rows 5 then 6). Shared Unit/Topic and the single 'denominations' token overlap alone would not suffice; the decision rests on the objective texts and their LCs. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are P1 (rank 0) Knowledge Objectives, so the grain requirement is met and same-rank direction rests on substantive content. The first SFI ('Identify numbers from 0 to 99', Unit 6, Numbers and Operations / Whole Numbers, under the Key Unit Competence on counting, reading, writing and ordering whole numbers 0-99) establishes recognition of numerals across exactly the 0-99 range. The second SFI ('Identify Rwandan currency from 1Frw to 100 Frw', Unit 9, Measurement / Rwandan Currency, under a Key Unit Competence on differentiating and solving problems with currency 1Frw-100Frw) applies numeral recognition in that same numeric range to a concrete measurement/money context, i.e. an applied extension rather than mere repetition of 'identify'. Proficiency in reading and identifying numbers to 99 plausibly supports success in identifying currency denominations up to 100Frw, so the supported direction is first to second; the reverse is not supported. Shared Grade ancestor, the single shared LC token 'identify', and weak local-rank proximity were treated as nomination signals only. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), so this remains an inferred curriculum-grounded judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are same-grain Knowledge Objectives in P1 Unit 4 'Numbers from 0 up to 20' under the same Key Unit Competence (count, read, write, order, compare, add and subtract whole numbers 0-20). The first states discovering and understanding the concept of numbers 0-20 (LC: 'Understand the concept of numbers from 0 up to 20'); the second requires mentally adding and subtracting numbers up to 20 (LCs: mental addition and mental subtraction within 20). Although both sit at rank P1, the substantive evidence is directional within the same number range: secure conceptual grasp of the quantities 0-20 supports the likelihood of success in performing mental computation over that same range, whereas mental arithmetic is not needed to form the number concept. Shared Unit, Topic Area and token overlap alone were not treated as sufficient; the pair-specific concept-to-operation extension grounds the direction.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are same-grain Attitudes and Values Objectives within the Measurement topic area: the P2 item (rank 1, Unit 7 Mass measurements 'Kg') is '– Appreciate the way of measuring with accuracy when buying goods', while the P3 item (rank 2, Unit 7 Capacity Measurements) is '– Promotes trustworthiness in measuring liquids'. The disposition is the same class — integrity and accuracy in practical measurement situations — and the P2→P3 coordinate direction accompanies a substantive affective deepening from personally valuing accurate measurement in a buying context to actively promoting trustworthiness when measuring, extended from mass to capacity quantities. Holding the earlier appreciation of accurate measurement plausibly supports success in the later, more outward-directed trustworthiness disposition, so the permitted lower-to-higher developmental direction is preferred over symmetric coherence. Confidence is tempered because the lexical/LC evidence overlap is thin (only 'measuring'; Jaccard ~0.07–0.14), the measured attributes differ (mass vs capacity), and both endpoints' source evidence is truncated with 24 omitted items each, so the full printed attitude context could not be inspected. Shared Topic Area, Unit number, and LC wording were treated only as nomination signals.

judgment.rationale: Both are P1 Knowledge Objectives (same grain, same rank 0) within Unit 9 'Rwandan currency from 1Frw to 100 Frw' under the Key Unit Competence to differentiate Rwandan currency and solve problems using it. The second SFI ('Understand the features of each coin from 1Frw to 100Frw') establishes recognition of individual coins and their denominations, which is the substantive content knowledge a pupil needs before the first SFI ('Interpret the word problems of the Rwandan currency') can be performed: interpreting currency word problems presupposes knowing which coins exist and what each is worth. The direction is therefore second_to_first, justified by the pair-specific increase in complexity (coin recognition -> applying currency knowledge to contextual word problems), not merely by the shared unit, page 51 proximity, or the generic 'currency'/'frw' LC tag overlap (shared SFI tokens are only 'of'/'the'). Same-rank direction rests on this content dependency; the direction is developmentally supportive, not an asserted mandatory teaching order. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), so the judgment rests on the full statement texts and hierarchy supplied.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are P3 (rank 2) Skills Objectives, so the comparison stays within one statement-type grain. Fluency with multi-digit whole-number multiplication plausibly supports success in applying the same operation to measured capacity quantities and conversions, so the developmental direction runs from the whole-number objective to the measurement application, not the reverse. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are same-grain Knowledge Objectives in the Measurement / Length Measurements sub-topic area. The second (P1, rank 0, Unit 8 'Measuring the length less than or equal to 10 m') asks pupils to solve simple problems about lengths of 10 m or shorter, with its Key Unit Competence covering measuring, comparing, adding and subtracting lengths up to 10 m. The first (P2, rank 1, Unit 5 'Length measurements: m, dm, and cm') requires explaining how to add and subtract length measurements not exceeding 10 m, within a KUC that extends to conversion and multiplication/division of length measurements. Facility with practical length problems within the same 10 m range at P1 plausibly supports success in articulating the addition/subtraction procedures for length at P2, a substantive deepening from informal problem solving to explanation of operations on measured lengths. Direction is lower-to-higher rank (P1 to P2), matching the permitted second_to_first. The first requires counting, reading and writing numbers up to 5000 (LCs: count/read/write numbers ≤ 5000); the second requires arranging those same numbers from lowest to greatest and vice versa (LCs: ascending and descending ordering). judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are same-grain Knowledge Objectives at the same resolved Grade coordinate (P1, rank 0) under the shared Whole Numbers sub-topic, so direction rests on pair-specific content rather than shared ancestry, code prefix, or the weak 'numbers' token overlap. The first states mental subtraction where the first term does not exceed 10 (Unit 3: Numbers from 0 up to 10, KUC add/subtract 0-10); the second requires explaining how to solve word problems involving numbers up to 50 (Unit 5: Numbers from 0 to 50, KUC add/subtract 0-50). This is a substantive extension: fluency in mental subtraction facts within 10 supports the computational reasoning needed to explain solutions of word problems over the broader 0-50 range, so proficiency in the first raises likelihood of success in the second. Direction is not reversible, since word-problem explanation to 50 presupposes rather than develops within-10 mental subtraction. Confidence is moderate because both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each) and the second objective's application/explanation focus is not identical in skill type to mental computation.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Knowledge Objectives (same statement-type grain) in Geometry shape units. The second SFI asks pupils to illustrate straight, closed, open, curved and zigzag/broken lines forming real objects (P2 Unit 10: Types of lines and angles, KUC on identifying and drawing lines and angles); the first asks pupils to draw a square, rectangle and triangle (P2 Unit 11: Square, rectangle, and triangle, KUC on identifying those shapes and calculating perimeter). judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are P2 (rank 1) Skills Objectives, so the grain matches and direction must rest on substantive evidence rather than shared rank or the common 'read/write' tokens. The second SFI (Unit 2, Numbers and Operations / Whole Numbers) establishes accurate reading and writing of numbers 0–500 in words and figures, with LCs 'Read numbers up to 500 in numerals and words' and 'Write numbers up to 500 in numerals and words'. The first SFI (Unit 6, Measurement / Capacity Measurements, Key Unit Competence on measuring and recording capacity in litres) requires reading and writing the amount of space a liquid occupies in a container, i.e. applying numeral reading/writing to quantify and record a measured capacity. Fluency in reading and writing whole numbers therefore supports success in recording capacity amounts, giving a directional second_to_first link rather than mere lexical overlap; the reverse direction is not supported. Confidence is moderated because the numeric-notation dependency is inferred from the measurement wording and both endpoints' source evidence (and the second endpoint's LC metadata) are truncated.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are P1 Knowledge Objectives (same statement-type grain) under Topic Area 'Numbers and Operations' / Sub-Topic Area 'Whole Numbers', at the same resolved Grade coordinate P1 (rank 0). The first states '– Identify numbers from 1 to 5.' (Unit 1: Numbers from 1 to 5, whose Key Unit Competence covers counting, reading, writing, comparing, ordering, adding and subtracting whole numbers 1 to 5); the second states '– Mentally add and subtract numbers less than or equal to 10.' (Unit 3: Numbers from 0 up to 10, Key Unit Competence covering operations on whole numbers 0 to 10, with LCs 'Mentally add numbers less than or equal to 10' and 'Mentally subtract numbers less than or equal to 10'). Same-rank direction is supported by substantive pair-specific evidence beyond shared wording: secure identification/recognition of the small number range 1–5 is the number-sense foundation that supports success in mentally computing sums and differences within the broader 0–10 range, which additionally requires mental operation fluency and an extended range. Direction is therefore first_to_second; no reverse or symmetric reading is better supported. Limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each) and ancestors carry merge context (repeated Grade/Topic/Sub-Topic headers merged), so unit sequencing is inferred from the visible unit titles and Key Unit Competences rather than a full source reading.

That is extension of the same procedural skill to a new number type, so competence with symbolic comparison of whole numbers supports success in symbolic comparison of unit fractions; the direction is supported by the substantive domain extension rather than by shared wording or shared LC tokens ('compare', 'symbols') alone. Same-rank coordinate means direction rests on this evidence, and both endpoints' source evidence is truncated, which limits corroboration.

The first requires using a place-value table to determine the place value of four-digit numbers (Unit 2, numbers to 5000); the second requires illustrating multiplication of a 3-digit number by a 2-digit number with products up to 10,000 (Unit 3). Beyond the shared parentage (which alone would not suffice), there is a pair-specific substantive dependency: correctly illustrating and recording multi-digit products up to 10,000 relies on secure place-value structure of four-digit numbers, and the syllabus situates the place-value objective in the earlier Unit 2 number range (≤5000) with the multiplication objective extending to the ≤10,000 range in Unit 3. Same-rank direction is therefore grounded in this conceptual support plus unit sequencing, not on rank proximity or token overlap (shared tokens were only 'of'/'the'/'digit'). judgment.rationale: Both are Knowledge Objectives at the same grain and same coordinate (Grade P3, rank 2) within P3 Unit 4 'Fractions having a numerator less than or equal to 10'. The first states the conceptual meaning of denominator (number of equal parts a whole is divided into) and numerator (how many parts are considered); its LCs make both explicit. The second requires using drawings or real objects to compare fractions with the same denominator using <, >, = — a comparison that rests precisely on interpreting the fixed denominator as equal-part size and the differing numerators as counts of those parts. This is a pair-specific conceptual-to-applied extension, so proficiency in the meaning of numerator/denominator substantively supports success in comparing same-denominator fractions, justifying same-rank developmental direction first_to_second rather than mere shared-unit or shared-token coincidence. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are P3 Grade Key Competence statements (same grain, same canonical coordinate P3, rank 2) under the merged 'P3 Mathematics' Grade node, so hierarchy and page proximity alone are only nomination signals. The substantive evidence is in the statement texts: the second SFI establishes counting, reading, writing, comparing/ordering whole numbers to 10 000 and fluent use of the four operations with 4-digit numbers, while the first SFI requires reading, writing and drawing fractions not exceeding a whole with denominators up to 10, including exercises and word problems. Fluency in whole-number reading/writing notation, comparison and the division/partitioning idea carried by the four operations supports success in representing and operating on fractional parts of a whole and in solving related word problems; the converse support is not evidenced. Same-rank direction is therefore grounded in this specific whole-number-to-fraction dependency rather than shared parentage or the generic token overlap ('read', 'write', 'whole'). Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated with 24 omitted evidence items each, so the full competence context is only partially visible; confidence is moderated accordingly.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Skills Objectives (same statement-type grain). Perimeter work substantively extends the earlier single-segment length measurement to measuring multiple sides of a figure and then combining those measures by computation, so P1 length-measurement proficiency plausibly supports success with P2 perimeter measurement/calculation. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are P3 Skills Objectives in the same statement-type grain under Unit 3 'Numbers from 0 to 10000' (Key Unit Competence covering counting through dividing whole numbers to 10000). The second SFI is decomposing a 4-digit number into ones, tens, hundreds and thousands (LC tags: 4-digit, decompose, place value); the first is dividing a 4-digit number (dividend up to 10000) by a divisor of 9 or less. Place-value decomposition of 4-digit numbers is the structural basis for partitioning a dividend and executing single-digit division within the same number range, so proficiency in decomposing supports success in dividing; the reverse dependency is not supported. Coordinates are equal (P3, rank 2), but the substantive conceptual dependency (place-value structure feeding a division procedure on identical 4-digit magnitudes), plus the source table ordering (row 5 decomposition before row 7 division), justifies the same-rank direction. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are same-grain Knowledge Objectives in the 'Types of lines and angles' Geometry unit. The second (P2, rank 1) is 'Compare the angles using <,> or =', situated in a P2 Key Unit Competence that already introduces acute and obtuse angles; the first (P3, rank 2) is 'Identify and describe the characteristics/properties of right, acute, and obtuse angles' within the P3 unit whose KUC extends to right angles and drawing/comparing. Comparing angle magnitudes with inequality symbols establishes the relative-size sense of angles that proficiency in classifying and describing angle types by their properties draws on, so the lower-rank P2 objective supports likely success on the higher-rank P3 objective (second_to_first). Direction follows the resolved P2→P3 coordinate ranks, not label wording or shared unit titles alone. judgment.rationale: Both are P1 (rank 0) Skills Objectives under the same Key Unit Competence 'count, read, write, compare, order, add and subtract whole numbers from 1 to 5', so the grain and statement type match. The second SFI (P2, rank 1, Unit 13 'Pictographs / Simple graphs', LC 'Find the number of objects represented on a given pictograph') establishes basic quantity reading from a pictograph. Direction is supported at the same rank by this operational dependency, not by shared Unit, Topic Area, wording, or shared LC tokens ('whole numbers', '5000') alone. Direction at equal rank is grounded in this specific conceptual dependency (place-value structure into magnitude comparison), not in source order or shared page 59 proximity, which are weak signals only. The second SFI is Unit 1 'Numbers from 1 to 5' ('Count, read, and write numbers from 1 to 5', LCs: count/read/write 1–5); the first is Unit 4 'Numbers from 0 up to 20' ('Count and list scholastic and household materials whose number does not exceed 20', LCs: count and list materials up to 20). Direction runs second (Unit 1, 1–5) to first (Unit 4, up to 20). Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each) and both carry upstream merge/audit context on their ancestors, so the judgment rests on the bounded objective text, LCs, and unit headers shown.

judgment.rationale: Both are P3 (rank 2) Skills Objectives under the same Key Unit Competence 'count, read, write, expand, decompose, order, compare, add, subtract... numbers less than or equal to 5000', so the statement-type grain matches. The first requires decomposing numbers ≤5000 into ones, tens, hundreds and thousands (LC tags: decompose, place value); the second requires adding numbers with and without carrying with sums ≤5000 (LCs explicitly separate 'with carrying' and 'without carrying'). Carrying is regrouping across those same place-value units, so proficiency in place-value decomposition within the same 0–5000 range substantively supports success in multi-digit addition with carrying, justifying a same-rank forward direction from decomposition to addition rather than mere shared-unit co-occurrence. Confidence is moderated because both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and the direction rests on same-rank pedagogical reasoning rather than an explicit sequencing statement.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are same-grain Key Unit Competence statements at the same resolved coordinate (Grade P2, rank 1) under the merged 'TOPIC AREA: GEOMETRY' parent, so shared ancestry and token overlap ('pupils will be able to identify', 'key unit competence') alone carry no weight. The pair-specific content does support a developmental direction: Unit 10 asks pupils to identify and draw different types of lines and acute/obtuse angles, while Unit 11 asks pupils to distinguish squares, rectangles and triangles from other geometrical shapes and calculate their perimeter. Recognising and drawing line types and angle types is the constituent vocabulary and drawing skill used to discriminate these polygons (equal/parallel sides, right versus non-right angles) and to measure side lengths for perimeter, so proficiency with Unit 10's lines-and-angles competence plausibly supports success with Unit 11's shape-identification and perimeter competence, not the reverse. Judgment rests on the bounded excerpts; both endpoints' source evidence is truncated and all endpoints and ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context (including merged P2 Grade and Geometry Topic Area labels), which limits certainty about wider unit content.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Knowledge Objectives in the same statement grain within SUB-TOPIC AREA: CAPACITY MEASUREMENTS under TOPIC AREA: MEASUREMENT, so the comparison is within-grain. First (P2, rank 1, Unit 6 'Standard unit of capacity measurements "litre"') asks pupils to explain how to compare the capacity of various containers of liquids — direct, non-numeric comparison of container capacity. Second (P3, rank 2, Unit 7 'Capacity Measurements', KUC extending to litre–millilitre conversion and operations) asks pupils to explain how to estimate the amount of liquid a container can hold in litres, which presupposes a sense of relative container capacity and adds quantification against a standard unit. This is substantive extension (qualitative comparison to unit-referenced estimation) across ranks P2→P3, so proficiency in the earlier objective supports success in the later one; direction follows lower-to-higher rank as permitted. Shared Topic/Sub-Topic wording and the single shared LC tag 'capacity' alone were not treated as sufficient; the conceptual progression in the objective texts carries the judgment. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Skills Objectives at the same grain and same coordinate (Grade P2, rank 1) under Unit 6 'Standard unit of capacity measurements "litre"'. Same-rank direction is supported by pair-specific content, not merely shared ancestry or the single shared token 'numbers': ordering numbers in increasing or decreasing order (LCs 'Order numbers in increasing order' / 'in decreasing order') establishes the sequencing of ascending/descending number sequences, whereas the second objective requires learners to analyse a given sequence of numbers below 100 and determine the constant interval between consecutive terms (LC 'Find the common difference used to make a given number pattern with numbers less than 100'). Proficiency in ordering numbers supports success in identifying the common difference, which adds the extra demand of quantifying the interval within a two-digit range; the reverse direction is not supported. Source rows (row 5 then row 6 of the same unit table, pages 45 and 46) are consistent with this but were not treated as decisive. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated and both carry upstream audit/merge context, so confidence is moderate.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are P3 (rank 2) Skills Objectives in the same statement-type grain under Unit 3 'Numbers from 0 to 10000'. First: 'Dividing a 4-digit number by a number less than or equal to 9. The dividend should not exceed 10000'; second: 'Subtract with or without borrowing the numbers less than or equal to 10000. The first term should not exceed 10000.' Beyond the shared unit/ancestors and heavy lexical overlap (which alone would not suffice), there is pair-specific procedural coherence: fluent multi-digit subtraction with borrowing within 10000 is the operation executed at each step of dividing a 4-digit dividend by a single-digit divisor, so proficiency in the subtraction objective supports success in the division objective. Same-rank direction is therefore lower-support-to-higher-complexity (second_to_first), consistent with the unit's key competence sequence 'add, substract, and divide whole numbers to 10000' and the source row order (row 6 subtraction, row 7 division). Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence and the pair nomination evidence are truncated, so only the bounded excerpts above were used; the direction rests on the stated operational dependency rather than an explicit syllabus prerequisite statement.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are same-grain Knowledge Objectives in TOPIC AREA: STATISTICS concerning pictographs. The first (P2, rank 1, Unit 13 'Pictographs / Simple graphs', LC: 'Explain how to make a pictograph for counting similar objects') establishes how a pictograph is constructed by counting similar objects. The second (P3, rank 2, Unit 14 'Pictograph used in counting', LCs: 'Identify the frequency of items in a category on a pictograph' and 'Determine which category has the most or fewest items on a pictograph') extends that base to extracting category frequencies and comparing categories — a substantive deepening from construction/counting to interpretation and comparison of represented data. Coordinate ranks are resolved and differ (P2 → P3), so the permitted lower-to-higher direction first_to_second applies; understanding how pictograph pictures stand for counted objects supports success in reading frequencies and comparing categories. Shared LC/tag token overlap ('pictograph') alone was not treated as sufficient; the substantive content relation carries the judgment. Endpoint source evidence is truncated for both SFIs (24 omitted evidence items each), so the full source may contain further detail, but the visible objective texts and LCs are unambiguous.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Knowledge Objectives (same statement grain) in the Measurement topic area, Sub-Topic Area 'Length Measurements', with resolved Grade coordinates P2 (rank 1) and P3 (rank 2), so any developmental direction runs lower-to-higher. The P2 objective is conceptual foundation work: 'Define the length', with LC 'Define length as a measurement'. The P3 objective substantively extends this to naming the full metric unit system for length (km, hm, dam, m, dm, cm, mm), within a P3 unit on the relationship between length measurements, whereas the P2 unit is limited to m, dm and cm. Knowing what length is as a measurable attribute plausibly supports success in identifying and distinguishing the expanded set of length units, so this is substantive deepening/broadening rather than generic repetition of shared 'length'/'measurement' tokens. Evidence limitations: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each) and all endpoints and ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context (merged Grade and Topic Area representatives); the P3 source text also contains a duplicated verb artifact ('Identify and identify'), which does not change the objective's meaning.

Shared Unit/Topic Area, the 'pictograph'/'statistics' LC tag overlap, and P2 rank proximity only nominated the pair. judgment.rationale: Both are P3 (rank 2) Skills Objectives under the same Key Unit Competence (Unit 11: square, rectangle, triangle, circle), so the statement-type grain matches. The first ('Draw a square, a rectangle, a triangle, and a circle.') establishes the basic construction skill for the four figures, including the shared learning component 'Draw a circle'. The second ('Draw a circle and identify its center, radius, and diameter') reuses that same circle-drawing component and extends it with the additional components 'Identify the center/radius/diameter of a circle', i.e. substantive deepening from producing a figure to naming its internal parts; proficiency in drawing the circle supports success in the extended objective. Same-rank direction is grounded in this pair-specific component containment-plus-extension (first's LCs are drawing-only; second adds three identification LCs), not on shared parent, unit, wording, or the row-5/row-6 source adjacency alone.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are same-grain Key Unit Competence statements at the same resolved coordinate (Grade P3, rank 2), so direction rests on substantive content rather than rank. The first (P3 Unit 1, Numbers and Operations / Whole Numbers) states pupils count, read, write, compare, order, add, subtract, multiply and divide numbers 0-2000; the second (P3 Unit 13, Algebra / Equation) requires pupils to find the missing number using the rules of counting, with its parent Unit explicitly scoped to 'missing numbers in addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division'. Fluency with counting and the four operations on whole numbers is precisely the proficiency needed to determine an unknown term in those same operations, an extension into early equation reasoning; hence first_to_second buildsTowards rather than mere symmetric coherence. The shared P3 Grade ancestor and generic 'Key unit Competence: Pupils will be able to' token/trigram overlap were treated as nomination only. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated with 24 omitted evidence items each, but the visible competence statements and Unit titles are sufficient and non-conflicting.

judgment.rationale: Both are same-grain P3 Skills Objectives under the same Unit 7 'Capacity Measurements' Key Unit Competence (same rank P3, gap 0), so direction rests on substantive content difference. The second SFI is the foundational hands-on skill ('Measure and compare the capacity of liquid containers in liters (l)'; LCs: measure / compare capacity in litres), confined to one unit and two operations. Ranks are identical (P2), but the intra-grade content extension from ×10 to ×100 provides the substantive same-rank evidence for the first_to_second direction. judgment.rationale: Both are P3 Key Unit Competences (same statement-type grain, same Grade rank 2), so direction requires substantive evidence beyond shared coordinate or wording. The first (Unit 1, Numbers and Operations / Whole Numbers) establishes counting, reading, writing, comparing, ordering, adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing whole numbers 0-2000. This is application/extension of the same operational repertoire into a new quantity domain, not mere lexical overlap; the reverse direction is not supported since length measurement is not needed for whole-number arithmetic. Evidence for both endpoints is the single KUC header statement with truncated source refs, which bounds but does not contradict this reading.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are same-grain Knowledge Objectives at the same P3 coordinate (rank 2) within Unit 2 'Numbers from 0 to 5000'. The first states using the place-value table to determine the place value of numbers composed of four digits; the second states explaining the division of a number composed of four digits by a divisor less than or equal to 9. Beyond the shared Unit/parent and 'four digits' wording (which alone would not suffice), there is pair-specific conceptual dependency: understanding and reading the place-value structure of a four-digit number is the conceptual basis for explaining division of such a number digit-by-digit (thousands, hundreds, tens, ones), so proficiency in the place-value objective supports success in explaining four-digit division. The reverse direction is not supported, since explaining division does not underwrite basic place-value identification. Evidence for both endpoints is partly bounded (source evidence truncated, 24 omitted source-evidence items each), so the judgment rests on the supplied statement texts and LC tags ('place value', 'place value table' vs 'division', 'four-digit').

Same-rank direction is supported by substantive content change rather than shared parentage alone: the first objective is concrete quantity representation — forming and drawing groups of objects whose number does not exceed 5 (LCs 'group various objects...', 'draw groups of various objects...') — while the second requires ordering whole numbers up to 5 using symbols of comparison (LC tags 'order', 'comparison symbols'), an abstract, symbolic comparison of the same number range. Reliable cardinality of object groups to 5 supports success in ordering those numbers symbolically; the printed table rows (row 5 grouping/drawing, row 6 comparing groups then ordering with symbols) corroborate this concrete-to-symbolic progression. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated and carries upstream merge/audit context (ancestors are merged repeated Grade/Topic Area/Sub-Topic Area headers), which limits but does not contradict the visible objective texts.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are same-grain Skills Objectives in Geometry line work. The first (P1, rank 0, Unit 10 'Location of objects and lines') asks pupils to draw straight lines and closed lines; the second (P2, rank 1, Unit 10 'Types of lines and angles') asks pupils to illustrate straight, closed, open, curved, and zigzag/broken lines that form objects located in and outside the classroom. This is substantive extension in the lower-to-higher grade direction: the P2 statement retains the P1 line types (its LCs include straight and closed lines) while adding open, curved, and zigzag/broken types and applying the representation to real objects in the environment. Proficiency in drawing straight and closed lines plausibly supports success in the broader, contextualised P2 illustration task, so a P1-to-P2 developmental direction is supported beyond the shared Unit label and 'straight/closed/lines' token overlap that merely nominated the pair.

judgment.rationale: Both are same-grain Grade Key Competence statements under the merged 'P2 Mathematics' grade node at the same canonical rank (P2, rank 1), so direction rests on substantive content, not rank. The second SFI establishes counting, reading, writing, ordering, decomposing whole numbers 0-1000 and operating (+, -, x, /) with three-digit numbers; the first SFI applies exactly that number range and those operations in a money context (Rwandan notes and coins from 1Frw to 1000Frw, exchanging money, and solving word problems involving addition and subtraction). Proficiency with three-digit number sense and addition/subtraction plausibly supports success in the money-valuation, exchange, and word-problem competence, which adds a real-world contextual layer rather than merely repeating the number work. Shared grade parent, page proximity, and stopword-level token/trigram overlap were treated as nomination signals only; the judgment rests on the described number-range and operation dependency. Endpoint source evidence is truncated and both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context, so confidence is moderate.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are same-grain Knowledge Objectives in the Measurement / Time Measurements sub-topic (Unit 9 in each grade). The second (P2, rank 1) objective 'Tell hours of a day' establishes the hour-based sense of daily time (LC tags: day, hours, time) within a P2 Key Unit Competence limited to o'clock and half past. The first (P3, rank 2) objective 'Say the time shown by a clockface or a digital watch' extends that foundation to reading time off two concrete instrument representations, consistent with the P3 Key Unit Competence on reading/writing clock-face and digital-watch times. Naming hours of the day plausibly supports success in stating the time shown on a clock face or digital display, so the lower-rank P2 item builds towards the higher-rank P3 item; direction follows the resolved P2->P3 coordinate ranks, not the technical UUID order. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each) and all hierarchy nodes carry upstream merge/audit context, so the judgment rests on the bounded statement text, LCs, and Key Unit Competence context.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Skills Objectives (same statement-type grain) in the Capacity Measurements sub-topic. The first (P2, rank 1, Unit 6 'Standard unit of capacity measurements "litre"') has pupils physically measure the capacity of various containers using a one-litre bottle; the second (P3, rank 2, Unit 7 'Capacity Measurements') has pupils write the capacity of measured containers in litre, centilitre and millilitre. The practical measuring skill with a single litre unit is the concrete basis for recording measured capacities, and the P3 statement substantively extends it by requiring symbolic recording across finer subunits (l, cl, ml), consistent with its Key Unit Competence on l-to-ml relationships. Direction is lower-to-higher rank (P2 to P3), matching the permitted first_to_second. Token/LC overlap ('capacity', 'containers', 'litre') alone was treated only as nomination evidence; the judgment rests on the statements' complementary measure-then-record progression. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated, so the full source may contain further detail not visible here.

The P2 objective establishes the underlying drawing construction skill for straight-sided plane figures whose corners are angles (notably the right angles of squares and rectangles), and the P3 objective extends that same drawing skill to producing and distinguishing specified angle types, a more analytic and complex geometric construction target. Grade coordinates are resolved and different (P2 -> P3), so the permitted developmental direction is lower-to-higher, first_to_second. The nomination rests partly on shared 'draw'/'geometry' tokens and rank proximity, which alone would not suffice, but the pair-specific substantive extension from drawing whole figures to drawing classified angles supports the direction; bounded source/LC truncation on both endpoints limits certainty, hence moderate confidence.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are P2 (rank 1) Knowledge Objectives in the same statement-type grain under Topic Area 'Numbers and Operations' / Sub-Topic Area 'Whole Numbers'. The second SFI asks pupils to 'show and explain the place value of each digit in numbers composed of 3 digits' (Unit 1, numbers 0-200); the first asks pupils to 'explain how to add and subtract numbers whose sum and first term does not exceed 500' (Unit 2). Beyond the shared ancestry and 'explain/numbers' wording overlap (which alone would not suffice), place-value understanding of three-digit numbers is the conceptual basis for explaining addition and subtraction with regrouping in the hundreds range, so proficiency in the second supports success in the first. Same-rank direction is grounded in this substantive conceptual dependency (3-digit place value to 3-digit addition/subtraction), not in unit or source ordering. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and ancestors carry merge context for repeated Grade/Topic/Sub-Topic labels, so unit-level scope is inferred from the retained excerpts only.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are P2 (rank 1) Grade Key Competences under the same 'P2 Mathematics' grade grouping, so grain matches and the shared parent alone is not the basis. Substantively, the first competence is recognition-level geometry: selecting a square and a rectangle from among other geometric shapes and citing everyday objects of similar shape. The second extends the same shape set (adding the triangle) to drawing the figures, stating their defining features, and calculating perimeter — a move from visual identification to property articulation and measurement computation. Reliable discrimination of squares and rectangles plausibly supports success in drawing and describing their features and in perimeter calculation, justifying a same-rank forward direction first_to_second rather than mere symmetric coherence. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (26 omitted items each) and one source_ref excerpt is cut off, so only the bounded statement text supports this reading.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are same-grain P3 Knowledge Objectives at the same canonical rank (P3), so direction rests on substantive content rather than rank. The second SFI ('Identify the place value of numbers composed of four digits', P3 Unit 1, Numbers and Operations / Whole Numbers, Key Unit Competence on counting, reading, writing and comparing numbers to 2000) establishes four-digit numeral place-value reading, which is the numeric knowledge needed to identify the printed values of Rwandan notes and coins from 1 Frw up to 5000 Frw in the first SFI (P3 Unit 8, Measurement / Rwandan Currency, Key Unit Competence on using up to 5000 Frw for buying and selling). Proficiency in reading four-digit place value therefore supports success in identifying money denomination values; this is an applied extension of number knowledge into currency, not mere repetition. Note the nomination's lexical overlap centres on the ambiguous token 'value' ('place value' vs 'money value'), and both endpoints have truncated source evidence (and truncated LC evidence for the second), so confidence is moderate rather than high; the shared P3 Grade ancestor alone was not treated as evidence.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Skills Objectives (same statement-type grain) in P2 Unit 6 'Standard unit of capacity measurements "litre"', and the merge audit confirms they are distinct printed objectives rather than duplicate extractions. The first establishes the basic measuring act — using a one-litre bottle as the unit to measure the capacity of various containers (LC: 'Measure the capacity of various containers using a one-litre bottle'). The second extends this to quantifying capacity up to 10 litres and additionally comparing containers in litres (LCs: 'Measure capacity up to 10 litres in litres (l)', 'Compare the capacity of liquid containers in litres (l)'). Proficiency in iterating the one-litre unit substantively supports success in measuring larger multi-litre amounts and comparing those measured capacities, which justifies a forward developmental direction despite the equal P2 rank. Shared Unit/Topic Area, page proximity, and token overlap were treated only as nomination signals; the direction rests on the unit-iteration-to-multi-unit-quantification-and-comparison extension in the visible source text. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Skills Objectives (same statement-type grain) in the 'Fractions' sub-topic area of 'Numbers and Operations'. The second SFI (P2, rank 1) asks pupils to compare the specific unit fractions 1/2, 1/4 and 1/8 using <, > or =; the first SFI (P3, rank 2) extends comparison to general same-denominator fractions with denominators up to 10 and adds addition and subtraction of such fractions (sum not exceeding a whole). This is a lower-to-higher rank progression with substantive broadening (from three named unit fractions to any same-denominator fractions ≤10) and extension into operations, so fluency in comparing simple unit fractions with symbols supports success with the P3 comparison and same-denominator arithmetic. Shared LC tokens ('compare','fractions') alone were not treated as sufficient; the fraction-magnitude comparison content itself carries the judgment. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated and both carry upstream merge/audit context (ancestor Grade and Topic Area nodes were merged headers), so the evidence is bounded, but the visible objective texts are unambiguous.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Skills Objectives (same grain) under TOPIC AREA: STATISTICS pictograph units. The second SFI (P2, rank 1, Unit 13 'Pictographs / Simple graphs', LC 'Complete a pictograph using the given information') requires pupils to construct/fill in a pictograph, establishing understanding of how symbols/groups represent quantities. The first SFI (P3, rank 2, Unit 14 'Pictograph used in counting', LCs 'identify the number of objects represented by each group on a pictograph' and 'find the group with the highest/lowest number of objects') extends this to reading off quantities per group and comparing groups to determine extremes — an interpretive and comparative step beyond completing a chart. Proficiency in constructing/completing pictographs plausibly supports success in extracting and comparing represented quantities, so the lower-to-higher rank direction (second_to_first) is supported; this is a curriculum-inferred progression, not empirical prerequisite truth. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are same-grain Knowledge Objectives about interpreting word problems: the first (Grade coordinate P1, rank 0) interprets word problems set in Rwandan currency from 1Frw to 100Frw (Measurement / Rwandan Currency, Unit 9), and the second (P2, rank 1) interprets word problems with whole numbers from 0 up to 1000 (Numbers and Operations / Whole Numbers, Unit 3). Direction is lower-to-higher rank, and the change is substantive rather than mere repetition: the P1 objective exercises word-problem interpretation in a concrete, small-value money context, while the P2 objective extends the same interpretive skill to a much larger and more abstract numeric range embedded in a unit covering counting, comparing, adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing to 1000. Proficiency in reading and interpreting the concrete currency word problems plausibly supports success with the broader numeric word problems, so a permitted buildsTowards is preferred over the symmetric option. Confidence is moderated because the two objectives sit under different Topic Areas (Measurement vs Numbers and Operations), so the link rests on the transferable word-problem interpretation skill rather than shared content domain, and both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted source-evidence items each), so unexcerpted source text was not available.

Same-rank direction here rests on the substantive procedural dependency, not on unit order or the shared 'subtract' token alone. judgment.rationale: Both are Skills Objectives at the same grain and same resolved coordinate (P3, rank 2) under Unit 6 'Mass measurements from kilogram (Kg) to gram (g)'. The second SFI states the concrete measuring procedure ('Measure the mass of different objects having a mass less than or equal to 10 kg without error and using balances'), while the first states the transfer/application ('Using mass measurements from kg to g in daily life'). Accurate hands-on measurement with balances is the operative skill that makes applying kg-to-g mass measurement in everyday contexts feasible, so proficiency in the second supports success in the first; the change is procedural mastery extended into real-life application, not mere repetition. Same-rank direction is grounded in this pair-specific procedural-to-application relationship rather than shared Unit/Topic Area or token overlap ('kg', 'mass'), which alone would not suffice. First states 'Show and explain the place value of each digit in numbers composed of 3 digits' (Unit 1: Numbers 0-200); second states 'Read and write numbers to the extent up to 500 in numerals and words' (Unit 2: Numbers 0-500), with LCs 'Read numbers up to 500 in numerals and words' and 'Write numbers up to 500 in numerals and words'. Understanding and explaining the place value of each digit in a 3-digit number substantively supports accurately reading and writing 3-digit numbers (up to 500) in numerals and words, where hundreds/tens/ones structure governs the numeral-to-word correspondence and the extended range. Direction at equal grade rank is supported by this conceptual dependency plus the Unit 1 (0-200) to Unit 2 (0-500) range broadening, not by unit order alone; shared ancestors and generic token overlap ('and', 'in', 'numbers') were treated as nomination signals only. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are P2 Knowledge Objectives (same grain, same rank P2) on place value of each digit in three-digit numbers, so the comparison is within-type and legitimate. The second SFI sits under Unit 1 'Numbers from 0 to 200' (Key Unit Competence limited to whole numbers 0–200), where 'show and explain' place value of 3-digit numbers is first introduced within a restricted range; the first SFI sits under Unit 2 'Numbers from 0 to 500' (Key Unit Competence to 500) and asks pupils to 'identify and explain' the place value of each digit in three-digit numbers across the broadened range. Same-rank direction rests on the unit-scope number-range evidence rather than on shared Topic/Sub-Topic Area, wording overlap, or shared LC tokens, which alone would not suffice; the overlap is near-duplicate in wording, which tempers confidence. judgment.rationale: Both are P2 (rank 1) Skills Objectives under the same Unit 3 'Numbers from 0 to 1000' Key Unit Competence, so grain and statement type match. Same-rank direction is supported by pair-specific content rather than shared parentage: the first SFI is place-value decomposition of numbers 1-1000 into ones, tens and hundreds (LC tags 'decompose', 'place value', 'hundreds'), while the second requires adding and subtracting with sums/first terms up to 1000 (LCs 'add numbers whose sum does not exceed 1000', 'subtract numbers whose first term does not exceed 1000'). Fluency in decomposing three-digit numbers by place value underpins the regrouping/column work needed for three-digit addition and subtraction, so proficiency in the first supports success in the second; the reverse dependency is not evidenced. Both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context and truncated source evidence (24 omitted items each), so the judgment rests only on the bounded excerpts and LCs shown.

judgment.rationale: Both are P1 Skills Objectives (same statement-type grain, same rank P1) in Unit 9 'Rwandan currency from 1Frw to 100 Frw'. The second SFI establishes recognition of the value and usage of coins/notes from 1Frw to 100Frw (LCs: 'show the value...', 'show the usage...'), while the first applies that knowledge to a more complex transactional judgment — deciding which items a given amount of money can buy (LC tags: money, purchasing). Knowing denominational value and usage substantively supports success in determining affordable purchases, so the same-rank direction runs second-to-first rather than the reverse. Shared Unit/Topic Area, page proximity, and the 'currency'/'frw' tag overlap only nominated the pair; the decision rests on the pair-specific value-recognition-to-application step. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), so the judgment rests on the bounded printed objective texts and LCs.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are same-grain Skills Objectives in the Measurement / Rwandan currency strand: the second (P1, rank 0, Unit 9 'Rwandan currency from 1Frw to 100 Frw') asks pupils to appropriately use currency from 1Frw to 100Frw when buying goods, while the first (P2, rank 1, Unit 8 'Rwandan currency from 1Frw to 1000Frw', Key Unit Competence on counting and exchanging currency to 1000Frw) asks pupils to plan how to use money up to 1000Frw and show how to save money. Direction is lower-to-higher rank and matches the only permitted buildsTowards direction. The change is substantive rather than mere repetition: the money range extends tenfold and the demand shifts from appropriate transactional use to planning and saving, so competent practical use of small-denomination currency in purchases supports success in budgeting and saving with larger amounts. Both endpoints' source evidence lists are truncated (24 omitted items each) and all involved SFIs carry upstream audit/merge context, so judgment rests on the supplied objective texts, LCs (shared 'currency', 'frw', 'money' tags), coordinates, and unit/topic ancestry.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are same-grain Skills Objectives at the same canonical Grade coordinate (P2, rank 1) under the same Key Unit Competence 'count, read, write, arrange, compare... whole numbers from 0 to 500'. The first requires accurate counting, reading and writing of numbers 1-500 (LCs: count/read/write numbers to 500); the second requires arranging numbers 0 to 500 in ascending and descending order (LCs: arrange ascending, arrange descending). Ordering a set of three-digit numerals presupposes fluent counting sequence knowledge and correct reading/writing of those numerals, so proficiency in the first substantively supports success in the second — a same-rank direction justified by the dependency of ordering on number naming/counting rather than by shared unit, wording, or page proximity alone. Evidence limits: pair nomination evidence and both endpoints' source evidence are truncated (24 omitted source-evidence items each), and all endpoints/ancestors carry upstream merge/audit context, so only the bounded visible objective text and LCs were used.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are same-grain Skills Objectives in the Measurement/Currency strand. The first (P2, rank 1, Unit 8 'Rwandan currency from 1Frw to 1000 Frw') asks pupils to select different denominations of Rwandan currency (notes and coins); the second (P3, rank 2, Unit 8 'Rwandan money from 1Frw to 5000 Frw') asks pupils to use money up to 5000 Frw in buying, selling, and exchanging activities (LCs: buying, selling, exchanging). Recognising and selecting denominations is the enabling handling skill for transacting with a larger money range, so proficiency in the P2 objective supports success in the broader, higher-range P3 application; direction follows the lower-to-higher grade coordinate. Endpoint and ancestor audit/merge context and truncated source evidence were noted but do not conflict with this reading.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Knowledge Objectives at the same grain and same P3 coordinate (rank 2) under Unit 2 'Numbers from 0 to 5000'. Same-rank direction is justified by this pair-specific conceptual dependency, not by the shared Unit/Topic/Key Unit Competence parent, shared 'numbers' token, or identical source page, which alone would be insufficient. judgment.rationale: Both are P3 Key Unit Competences (same statement-type grain, same coordinate rank 2). The second SFI (Unit 1, Numbers and Operations / Whole Numbers) states pupils count, read, write, compare, order, add, subtract, multiply and divide numbers 0-2000; the first SFI (Unit 8, Measurement / Rwandan Currency) requires pupils to use Rwandan money up to 5000 Frw appropriately for buying and selling. Handling money amounts in transactions depends on the whole-number comparison, ordering and four-operation fluency described in the Unit 1 competence, so proficiency in the number competence supports success in the money-application competence; the money unit also extends the range (to 5000 Frw) and applies the skills in a real-world measurement context. Direction is therefore second_to_first at equal grade rank on substantive conceptual grounds, not on the shared Grade ancestor, shared boilerplate tokens ('pupils will be able', 'key unit competence') or local rank proximity, which alone would not establish a relation. Both endpoints' source evidence is bounded/truncated (24 omitted items each), so the judgment rests on the supplied competence statements.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are P2 (rank 1) Knowledge Objectives under the same Key Unit Competence on time measurement (Unit 9: Hours, Months of the Year, Days in Each Month), so the grain and statement-type constraint is satisfied. Beyond shared placement, there is pair-specific instructional coherence with a defensible same-rank direction: the second SFI ('Tell hours of a day', LC tags day/hours/time) establishes the basic capacity to name and read hours within a day, while the first SFI ('Explain how to plan daily and weekly activities as well as time management', LCs on planning daily/weekly activities and managing time) applies hour-level time knowledge to organising activities across a day and week. Proficiency in telling the hours of a day plausibly supports success in explaining daily/weekly planning and time management, which is the broader, applied objective; the reverse support is not evidenced. Direction rests on this substantive content difference, not on shared ancestors, page proximity, or the single shared LC token 'time'. Note both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all context nodes carry merge/audit context, so the judgment is bounded by the excerpts supplied.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are same-grain Key Unit Competences at the same canonical coordinate (Grade P2, rank 1) under the merged Topic Area 'Numbers and Operations'. The first (Unit 1, Sub-Topic Area Whole Numbers) requires pupils to count, read, write, compare, arrange, add/subtract and multiply/divide whole numbers 0-200; the second (Unit 4, Sub-Topic Area Fractions) requires pupils to read, write, draw, compare and shade 1/2, 1/4 and 1/8. The whole-number competence is the broader foundational one and the fraction competence is the narrower extension, and the source Unit ordering (Unit 1 before Unit 4 within P2) is consistent with that same-rank direction. judgment.rationale: Both are P3 Skills Objectives (same grain, same rank 2) under Unit 10 'Types of lines and angles' and the same Key Unit Competence, so the shared parentage alone is not decisive. The pair-specific content, however, shows a substantive conceptual progression: the first asks pupils to show straight parallel, perpendicular and intersecting lines on materials in and outside the classroom (LCs tagged parallel/perpendicular/intersecting lines), while the second asks pupils to show right, acute and obtuse angles on objects in and outside the classroom (LCs tagged right/acute/obtuse angle). Angles in the environment are recognised where lines meet or intersect, and perpendicularity is defined by the right angle, so fluency in spotting intersecting/perpendicular lines on real objects directly supports the harder discrimination of angle types on those same objects; the Key Unit Competence and the source table also present lines (row 5, page 132) before angles (row 6, page 133). Direction is first (lines) to second (angles); no reverse dependency is evidenced. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated and both carry upstream audit/merge context, which limits certainty but does not contradict this reading.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Knowledge Objectives in the same statement-type grain within Topic Area 'Numbers and Operations' / Sub-Topic Area 'Whole Numbers'. The second SFI (P2, rank 1, Unit 2 'Numbers from 0 to 500') states 'Explain how to compare and order numbers less than or equal to 500', while the first SFI (P3, rank 2, Unit 3 'Numbers from 0 to 10000') states 'Compare numbers less than or equal to 10,000'. This is the same comparison concept extended to a substantially larger number range (500 to 10,000), with the P3 Key Unit Competence adding place value to four digits; understanding comparison of three-digit numbers supports success in comparing four-digit numbers. Direction is lower-to-higher rank (P2 to P3), i.e. second_to_first, consistent with the permitted direction. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated and carries upstream merge/audit context, so the judgment rests on the visible objective statements, LC tags ('compare','numbers') and resolved grade coordinates rather than full source text.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are P1 Knowledge Objectives (same statement-type grain, same coordinate rank 0) within Numbers and Operations > Whole Numbers. The second SFI defines place value of digits in numbers not exceeding 50 (Unit 5: Numbers from 0 to 50), while the first defines place value of digits in numbers not exceeding 99 (Unit 6: Numbers from 0 to 100), whose Key Unit Competence extends counting/reading/comparing/adding whole numbers to 99. This is a pair-specific substantive extension of the same place-value concept to a larger two-digit range within the same grade, so proficiency with place value to 50 supports success with place value to 99; the within-grade unit sequence (Unit 5 before Unit 6) and widened numeric scope provide the substantive same-rank direction evidence beyond mere wording overlap.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are same-grain Skills Objectives under the same P1 Unit 2 Key Unit Competence ('count, read, write, order, compare, add, and subtract whole numbers from 1 to 9'), so shared hierarchy only nominates. The substantive pair-specific difference is representational level: the first compares concrete groups of objects with quantities not exceeding 9, while the second compares numbers up to 9 using the formal comparison symbols <, > and = (LC tags 'comparison symbols'). Success with concrete quantity comparison of object groups directly supports the abstraction of the same comparison relation into symbolic notation, which is a genuine developmental deepening rather than mere repetition; the source rows (row 5 then row 6) are consistent with this ordering. Same coordinate rank (P1) is not the basis for direction; the concrete-to-symbolic shift is. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and ancestors carry merge context, but the visible statement texts and LC claims are unambiguous for this judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are P2 (rank 1) Knowledge Objectives under the same Unit 3 'Numbers from 0 to 1000' Key Unit Competence, so the grain matches. The second SFI concerns identifying and explaining the place value of each digit in three-digit numbers; the first concerns describing multiplication of 0–10 by 6, division of numbers up to 60 by 6, and multiplication of 0–100 by 10 with products up to 990. The multiplication-by-10 component depends directly on understanding the place-value shift and reading of three-digit results, and the divide/multiply work spans the hundreds range the place-value objective defines; proficiency in three-digit place value therefore supports success in the multiplication/division objective rather than the reverse. Direction at equal rank is supported by this pair-specific conceptual dependency, not by shared ancestors, the single shared token 'numbers', or adjacent table rows/pages, which alone would not suffice. Source evidence excerpts for both SFIs and the second SFI's LC metadata are truncated, so the judgment rests on the visible full objective statements.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Skills Objectives in the Fractions sub-topic area of Numbers and Operations, so the same-grain constraint is met. The first (P2, rank 1, Unit 4 'Fractions 1/2, 1/4 and 1/8') is the concrete partitioning skill of dividing a real object into 2, 4 and 8 equal parts; the second (P3, rank 2, Unit 4 'Fractions having a numerator less than or equal to 10') requires working out mathematical problems involving fractions of a whole number or of a given number of objects. Physically partitioning a whole into equal parts establishes the equal-share meaning of a unit fraction that P3 problem solving applies quantitatively to whole numbers and sets of objects, so proficiency in the earlier skill supports success in the later one across a lower-to-higher grade rank gap. This is a substantive extension (concrete equal-partition action to applied fraction-of-a-quantity problem solving), not mere shared 'fractions' wording; the token/trigram overlap evidence ('a', 'obj') is negligible and was not relied on.

Fluency with whole-number multiplication is the computational procedure re-used when operating on length quantities, so proficiency in the first plausibly supports success in the second (context-extension, not mere shared vocabulary). Shared Grade ancestor and the single 'multiply' token overlap alone were not treated as sufficient; the KUC-level requirement of multiplying measurements by a whole number carries the judgment. Confidence is moderate because the second objective is broader than multiplication and both source-evidence sets are truncated.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are same-grain P2 Skills Objectives under the same Topic Area (Numbers and Operations) and Sub-Topic Area (Whole Numbers), so the shared hierarchy alone is only a nomination trigger. The pair-specific evidence is substantive: the second SFI ('Count without mistakes, read and write numbers from 1 to 200', Unit 1: Numbers from 0 to 200) establishes secure counting, reading and writing of the numeral system within a 0–200 range, while the first SFI ('Decompose numbers from 1 to 1000 into ones, tens, and hundreds', Unit 3: Numbers from 0 to 1000, LC tagged 'place value') both extends the number range and adds an explicitly place-value structural operation on three-digit numbers. Fluent reading/writing of multi-digit numerals plausibly supports success at decomposing numbers into hundreds, tens and ones, so the developmental direction runs from the second to the first endpoint. Same canonical rank (P2) means direction rests on this unit-sequence and range/complexity extension rather than on rank; source evidence for both endpoints is truncated, which moderates confidence.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are same-grain P3 Knowledge Objectives at the same resolved Grade rank (P3), so direction rests on substantive content rather than rank. The second SFI (Unit 3, Numbers and Operations / Whole Numbers, 'Identify the place value of each digit in a four digit numbers', within a Key Unit Competence covering reading, writing, comparing whole numbers to 10000) develops four-digit numeral reading and place-value understanding; the first SFI (Unit 8, Measurement / Rwandan Currency, 'Identify the value of Rwandan money from 1 Frw up to 5000 Frw', Key Unit Competence on using up to 5000 Frw for buying and selling) applies numeral value recognition to currency denominations wholly inside the 0–10000 range. Proficiency in place value of four-digit numbers plausibly supports success in identifying and comparing monetary values up to 5000 Frw, and the within-grade unit ordering (Unit 3 before Unit 8) is consistent with that support. The shared lexical token 'value' carries different senses (place value vs monetary value) and the shared Grade ancestor alone was not treated as evidence; the judgment rests on the numeric-magnitude dependency, which moderates confidence. Source evidence for both endpoints and LC evidence for the second are truncated, so the full objective context is only partially visible.
